title: Russia’s Navy Shows Its Reach Around Japan’s Southwestern Islands
author: Christopher Woody
text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin visits the Yasny fish processing complex on Iturup island, Aug. 13, 2026.
Credit: Russian Presidential Press and Information Service
President Vladimir Putin’s mid-August visit to the Kuril Islands, his first as Russia’s leader, inflamed a decades-old territorial dispute with Japan and drew worldwide attention to the two countries’ border in the northern Pacific. But over the past several years, Russian forces have been increasingly active far to the south, around Japan’s southwestern-most islands, in a demonstration of the Russian military’s reach and its willingness to challenge its rivals on its own and alongside China.The dispute centers on the southernmost islands in the Kuril chain, which Japan calls its Northern Territories and says the Soviets seized illegally after Tokyo’s surrender at the end of World War II. Thousands of former Japanese residents of the islands are still alive, and resolving the dispute is a high priority for Japanese leaders. Russia’s activity on the islands, especially its military buildup, is therefore a sensitive issue for Tokyo.[...]
